description: Pre-registration Microsoft sign-in walled garden: devices on MFA-protected owned domains can now complete Microsoft password+Authenticator sign-in (device-code flow) BEFORE having internet access. A new preauth-relay container intercepts PORTAL_IP:443 ahead of NPM, forwards allow-listed Microsoft identity SNIs to the internet, and passes all other TLS (including the portal itself) through to NPM. The Microsoft device_code is now held server-side (sqlite) and never sent to the browser. installer.sh deploys and verifies the relay on every run.

add.description: Pre-auth Microsoft sign-in relay (preauth-relay container). 'auto' (default) enables it when DOMAIN_AUTH_PROVIDERS is set; 1/0 force on/off. When active it inserts a nat REDIRECT of PORTAL_IP:443 to the relay port and SNI-routes Microsoft identity hostnames upstream.
Local listen port for the pre-auth SNI relay.

Override the relay's built-in Microsoft identity hostname allow-list (comma-separated; '*.suffix' allowed). Leave empty to use the built-in list. Only add hostnames confirmed via DENY-SNI entries in the preauth-relay log; never add generic CDN/Azure wildcards.

notes: After upgrading each site: (1) docker compose build dnsmasq-hijack && docker compose up -d dnsmasq-hijack preauth-relay (or just re-run installer.sh, which deploys and verifies the relay); (2) restart the captive-portal web container — this applies the handle-based device-code store AND pushes the updated ACL baseline to every switch (hp5130-acl-baseline.sh now owns ACL 3000/PREAUTH on the wired VLAN, including 443 to HIJACK_DNS_IP for the relay; no manual switch commands); (3) the hijack dnsmasq now answers Microsoft identity domains with HIJACK_DNS_IP (everything else stays on PORTAL_IP) and the relay intercepts only HIJACK_DNS_IP:443 — portal traffic goes direct to NPM so the portal always sees real client IPs; (4) test from an UNREGISTERED device: the portal loads without 'Remote Access Not Supported', https://microsoft.com/devicelogin completes password+Authenticator sign-in, https://example.com does NOT load, raw-IP HTTPS fails; (5) watch 'docker logs preauth-relay' for DENY-SNI lines — if Microsoft's flow needs an extra hostname, add it via PREAUTH_ALLOWED_SNI (it feeds both the relay allow-list and the dnsmasq split answers). No DB migration. Rollback: set PREAUTH_HTTPS_RELAY_ENABLED=0, then docker compose up -d preauth-relay && docker compose restart dnsmasq-hijack.
